label: PF Backlog 439
title: /pf command: build mode only (not orchestrator) + global /pf for all opencode sessions
body:
## Problem / why
The `.opencode/command/pf.md` frontmatter binds every `/pf <verb>` invocation to the `orchestrator` agent (`agent: orchestrator` + `model: opencode-go/mimo-v2.5`), so deterministic thin-client verbs (backlog list, status, ...) run in the orchestrator agent instead of build mode. `.opencode/command/pipeline.md` has the same binding. Also, `/pf` exists only inside the product-forge repo - opencode sessions in other directories have no `/pf` command at all.

## Goal & value
- `/pf ...` always executes in build mode (`agent: build`), with no model pin so the session's model is inherited.
- `/pf ...` available in EVERY opencode session via the global command dir, calling `scripts/pf.py` by absolute path (pf.py self-locates ROOT, so any cwd works).

## In scope / Out of scope
In: frontmatter of `.opencode/command/pf.md` and `.opencode/command/pipeline.md`; new global command `$USERPROFILE/.config/opencode/command/pf.md`. Plus `/pf help [verb]` usage details (help registry + renderer in `scripts/pf.py`).
Out: `scripts/pipeline.py`, agent definitions, and installer (install.py/install.sh/install.bat) wiring.

## User flow
User runs `/pf backlog list` in any opencode session (any cwd) -> command executes under the build agent -> JSON output reported.

## Backend flow (consumed, by id)
`/pf <verb>` -> `scripts/pf.py <verb>` (thin client) -> canonical core/API. No orchestration in the command file (guard: scripts/dev/pf_surface_check.py).

## Acceptance criteria (testable G/W/T)
- GIVEN the project `pf.md` WHEN its frontmatter is read THEN `agent: build` is present and `agent: orchestrator` / `model:` are absent.
- GIVEN a session outside the repo WHEN `/pf help` is invoked THEN it resolves to the global command and runs pf.py by absolute path.
- GIVEN `/pf help` WHEN run THEN the overview lists every verb with its usage line (exit 0).
- GIVEN `/pf help <verb>` WHEN run THEN subcommands + flags for that verb are printed (exit 0);
  an unknown topic exits 2 with the verb list.
- GIVEN the repo WHEN `python scripts/dev/pf_surface_check.py` runs THEN it exits 0.

## Data model (what is stored, where, owner)
Command frontmatter: `.opencode/command/*.md` (project) and `~/.config/opencode/command/*.md` (global). Single writer: this item's implementation.

## API contract (endpoints and payloads)
None - surface-level change (clients only; API untouched).

## UX (screens / elements / states)
`/pf` slash command available in the command palette of every session.

## Edge cases and errors
- Global vs project command with the same name: project overrides global inside the repo - both are kept in sync at `agent: build`.
- Paths with spaces: absolute pf.py path must be quoted in the global command body.

## Dependencies and links (by id)
BI-PF-0372 (P10 /pf umbrella surface, completed).

## Open questions
None.

## Verification / test plan
python scripts/dev/pf_surface_check.py; python -m compileall -q core scripts dashboard; python scripts/dev/wired_audit.py; manual /pf help in a fresh session after opencode restart. python scripts/pf.py help | help backlog | help nope (exit 0/0/2).

analysis.implementation_strategy: MODIFY the frontmatter of .opencode/command/pf.md and .opencode/command/pipeline.md (agent: build, drop model pin); NEW global command file ~/.config/opencode/command/pf.md that invokes scripts/pf.py by quoted absolute path (pf.py already self-locates ROOT). EXTEND scripts/pf.py with a help registry + renderer (verb -> usage line, subcommands, flags) returning exit 0 for known topics and exit 2 with verb list for unknown topics. Reuse the existing thin-client verb dispatch and the guard scripts/dev/pf_surface_check.py (extend it to assert agent: build and absence of model pin).
dependency_findings: REQUIRES BI-PF-0372 (completed) - the /pf umbrella surface must exist.
RELATED BI-PF-1193 (docs correction for /pf) - keep help text consistent with run_pipeline.py vs pipeline.py naming.
Guard scripts/dev/pf_surface_check.py already exists and must be extended, not rebuilt.
conflict_findings: Single writer for .opencode/command/*.md frontmatter claimed by this item; no other open item appears to touch these files.
Global command file ~/.config/opencode/command/pf.md is a new path with no known concurrent writer.
duplication_findings: BI-PF-0372 (completed) built the /pf umbrella surface; this item is a follow-up correction, not a duplicate.
Related BI-PF-1193 (docs fix for /pf delegation) touches docs only; coordinate wording but no overlap in frontmatter or help renderer.
No existing help-registry component found; candidate components (core/agent_model_override.py, core/cost_model.py etc.) are unrelated to the CLI surface.
analysis.rationale: Small, well-scoped surface change: frontmatter edits, one new global command file, and a help renderer in the existing thin client. No API or data-model impact. Reuses the established /pf umbrella (BI-PF-0372) and the existing surface-check guard.
assumptions: pf.py self-locates ROOT from its own file location, so an absolute-path invocation from any cwd works.
opencode resolves project commands over global commands when both define /pf.
~/.config/opencode/command/ is the correct global command directory on the target platforms (Windows profile path noted as $USERPROFILE in the item).
risks: Project vs global command collision inside the repo - mitigated because project overrides global and both are kept in sync at agent: build.
Absolute path with spaces in global command body - must be quoted; verify manually on Windows and Linux.
opencode restart required for the global command to appear; not verifiable in CI.
Help renderer must stay in sync with verb dispatch - drift risk if verbs are added without updating the registry; mitigated by a surface-check assertion.
evidence: Item states pf.py self-locates ROOT; scripts/dev/pf_surface_check.py already exists as the guard harness.
Candidate components listed (core/agent_model_override.py etc.) are model/cost modules unrelated to the slash-command surface, confirming no reusable help renderer exists.

Whether /pf help should also list pipeline verbs or only pf verbs.
